reports.title: Eurostat Report on Mission Expenses
reports.description: Eurostat's own Methodology page: 'In the EU context, with effect from 2014 the mission expense values for hotel ceilings and for daily subsistence allowances are regularly reviewed on the basis of a Eurostat report.' (ERR-10). Sets hotel ceilings and daily subsistence allowances for EU staff on official mission travel. Publications page lists five linked reports (2015, 2019, 2021, 2024, 2026) under file titles varying informally by year: 'Eurostat Report on Mission Expenses' (2024), 'Eurostat Mission Expenses Report 2021' (2021).
reports.cadence_note: No document read states a fixed periodicity -- 'regularly reviewed' (Methodology page) is present-tense but not numeric. releases_per_year is an approximation from the observed publication record: five reports across 2015-2026 (an eleven-year span), at irregular intervals (4, 2, 3, 2 years). See ERR-10's own NOTES for the full reasoning; this is the branch's first EU node cadenced this way rather than from a stated rate.

release_schedule.note: Eurostat's Methodology page states mission-expense values (hotel ceilings, daily subsistence allowances) are 'regularly reviewed on the basis of a Eurostat report' but gives no numeric periodicity, calendar, or stated rule for when reviews occur. The Publications page lists a 'Mission expenses report' section but with no consistently dated release calendar found. This confirms the existing corpus note: five reports across 2015-2026 at irregular intervals (4, 2, 3, 2 years), with no fixed schedule.

dependencies.basis: Eurostat Methodology page, 'Mission expenses' section (ERR-11): 'Where possible the updating methodology uses information already established, including relevant sub indices of the harmonised index of consumer prices (to measure temporal evolution) and purchasing power parities (to measure spatial differences).' 'Uses information already established, including... the harmonised index of consumer prices' is a direct input statement, not a Research.1.md §5a 'comparable with' trap -- same shape as the rent survey's 'based on' language.
